title: What shielding does
purpose: Teach how matter, especially water, slows fast protons, what a model storm dose looks like behind thicker walls, and that dose never reaches zero.

beats.label: model
beats.credit: NASA (Clowdsley 2021) · model of the August 1972 solar storm

captions: Fast protons lose energy as they push through anything in their way.
Water is great at this, because it is packed with light hydrogen atoms.
The thicker the wall, the fewer get through.
A model of a huge 1972 solar storm shows what thicker shielding does.
Behind the thinnest wall, about {d5} mSv. Behind the thickest, about {d15}.
Thicker walls cut the dose, but it never drops to zero.
So crews do three things: put shielding up, get behind it fast, and stay there.
ends_on: Every layer of water helps, but only if it is in place before the protons arrive.

literals.why: the August 1972 solar particle event that Clowdsley 2021 models (fixture key aug1972_spe)
